title: Fall is the Home Stretch for Roth Conversions
subtitle: Today is the autumnal equinox. You have roughly 100 days to convert pre-tax dollars to Roth before December 31 — and lock in this year's tax bracket.
source_irs: IRC §408(d)(2); Form 8606 Part II; IRS Pub 590-B

concepts.heading: The 100-Day Window
concepts.lede: From September 22 (autumnal equinox) to December 31, you have about 100 days to convert pre-tax dollars to Roth and count them against this year's income.
body: A conversion is taxed in the calendar year it happens. Convert in 2026, it counts as 2026 income.
The deadline isn't a specific date — it's 'before midnight on Dec 31'.
Converting in the last week of December is the most common, and the most likely to be done in a panic.

concepts.heading: Lock In This Year's Bracket
concepts.lede: Markets down? Income down? That's the best time to convert. The lower your bracket this year, the cheaper the conversion.
body: Estimate your 2026 taxable income now. Subtract deductions. Find your bracket.
If you have room between your projected income and the top of your bracket, convert up to that amount.
$50,000 converted at 22% saves ~$11,000 vs. converting at 32% in a future year.

concepts.heading: Track on Form 8606
concepts.lede: Every conversion needs to be reported on Form 8606 Part II. Skip it, and the IRS assumes your conversion was 100% earnings (taxable + 10% penalty if early).
body: Form 8606 Part II: each conversion is a line — date, amount, basis carried over.
The 5-year clock starts on January 1 of the year AFTER the conversion.
Convert early in the year, before you forget. October is the sweet spot.
